_comment: Sites the plan's retired status was made for: gone from the code, not coming back.
These IDs were orphaned when the extractor learned to resolve Go string constants.
A site ID hashes path plus normalised SQL, so folding a constant into the golden
renumbers the site. The old entry recorded a golden of the form
'SELECT {{expr}} FROM ...' - which is not a statement anyone wrote, but what the
extractor produced before it could resolve the constant. Nothing was converted and
nothing was skipped: the entry described a statement that never existed.
Without this the burn-down reports them as conversions with no parity test, which
is the correct reading of the data and the wrong reading of the situation.

retired.reason: Superseded when the extractor learned to resolve Go string constants. Its golden was an unresolved-constant artefact (SELECT {{expr}} FROM mod_configs WHERE createdby = ? UN...), not real SQL. The same statement in modconfig/modconfig.go is now inventoried under a new id with the constant folded in, and is converted or triaged there.

The extractor matched it because "start" is the first word of START TRANSACTION and the generic method name Query is not unique to GORM. It was inventoried with a goldenSql of "start" and recorded as a keep-raw decision by two agents independently, which made it a deliberate-looking decision about a statement that does not exist. The extractor now requires a database receiver when the leading verb is also an ordinary word; see ambiguousLeadingKeyword in extract.go.
